title: Novartis ranks first place in 2026 Access to Medicine Index
body_markdown:
- *Novartis retains first place ranking among 20 sector peers for efforts to improve access to medicines*
- *First company to achieve No. 1 rank across all Technical Areas since Index began in 2008, achieving R&D score almost twice the sector average*
- *Recognizes progress to expand care for cancer and heart disease, Coartem® Baby, and next-gen antimalarial KLU156 (ganaplacide/lumefantrine)*


**Basel, November 10, 2026** – Novartis today announced the company has ranked first place in the 2026 Access to Medicine Index. Published every two years, the Index is an independent assessment of how major research-based pharmaceutical companies are improving access to medicines.


“Being ranked first in the Access to Medicine Index for the second consecutive time is an honor, and a recognition of our continued efforts to expand access to healthcare together with our partners,” said Vas Narasimhan, CEO of Novartis. “We remain committed to transforming scientific progress into meaningful impact for more patients around the world.”


The ranking retains Novartis’ leading position in the Index since 2024, with the company scoring an overall 3.86 out of five in 2026. Novartis also ranked first across all individual Technical Areas assessed, the only company to do so since the Index was first published in 2008, including a score for R&D almost twice the sector average.


The Index is published by the Access to Medicine Foundation, an independent non-profit organization, which assesses 20 of the world’s largest research-based pharmaceutical companies on their efforts to improve access to medicines, vaccines and diagnostics across 84 diseases across 113 low- and middle-income countries.¹


Companies were assessed on three Technical Areas in 2026: Governance of Access, which scores how companies embed accountability for access; Research & Development, which evaluates R&D activity and access planning for diseases affecting low- and middle-income countries; and Product Delivery, which tracks how companies reach patients and address barriers to access.


In 2025, Novartis reached 304 million patients worldwide. Of these, 30 million were reached through access approaches, including 7.3 million through the company’s dedicated Sub-Saharan Africa Business Unit.²˒³ Since the last Index in 2024, Novartis has:


- [Expanded](https://www.novartis.com/news/media-releases/novartis-announces-expansion-community-health-programs-close-gaps-heart-disease-and-cancer-care-targeting-more-30-countries-2030) community health programs to tackle the growing burden of chronic conditions like cancer and heart disease: Inclusive Health Accelerators, bringing screening and care closer to underserved communities in the U.S.; Community Health Initiatives in low- and middle-income countries, expanding diagnosis and treatment beyond traditional healthcare channels in hard-to-reach areas; and CARDIO4Cities, using data and partnerships to improve cardiovascular health in cities
- [Launched](https://www.novartis.com/news/media-releases/novartis-receives-approval-first-malaria-medicine-newborn-babies-and-young-infants) Coartem® Baby (artemether-lumefantrine), the first malaria treatment designed for newborns and young infants, with approval granted in 16 countries to date
- Completed submission of KLU156 (ganaplacide/lumefantrine), the first next-generation antimalarial, to Swissmedic and the U.S. FDA and received priority review
- Introduced more Emerging Market Brands, innovative medicine brands specifically designed to speed up access and address affordability challenges in low- and middle-income countries
- Renewed a landmark[agreement](https://www.novartis.com/stories/how-novartis-helping-eliminate-leprosy) with the World Health Organization to provide leprosy treatments at no cost
- Expanded a[partnership](https://www.novartis.com/stories/25-years-expanding-access-cancer-care) with the Max Foundation to improve access to care for cancer and other chronic diseases, across 6 treatments in 71 low- and middle-income countries
- Advance the development of new treatments for malaria and neglected tropical diseases, such as dengue, leishmaniasis and Chagas disease, backed by more than USD 500 million investment in R&D for global health since 2021⁴
